title: TrailGenic Altitude Terrain Physiology Comparison Dataset
description: Shell dataset module comparing physiological responses across different terrain and altitude conditions during endurance hiking.

records.mechanism: Technical terrain forces slower deliberate movement that keeps the system in a deeper aerobic zone

stimulus.terrain_context: technical alpine terrain versus smoother nontechnical routes

physiological_response: Technical terrain predicted +8.6 ms higher Day-2 HRV after controlling for adaptation.
Slower deliberate movement reduced cardiac volatility and kept output in a deeper aerobic zone.
Terrain complexity can increase muscular coordination demand while lowering systemic autonomic cost.
adaptation_outcomes: Technical terrain is not automatically a higher recovery cost when pacing is constrained.
Route difficulty must be separated into cardiac, muscular, terrain, and thermal components.
Technical alpine efforts may support recovery-positive aerobic loading after adaptation.

supporting_science.finding: Terrain slope and surface alter locomotion cost and movement economy.
Energy cost of locomotion increases significantly with slope and terrain variability.
